newsitem.title: POLAND: DEUTSCHE BANK POLSKA TO BREAK EVEN, EXPAND IN '97.
newsitem.headline: DEUTSCHE BANK POLSKA TO BREAK EVEN, EXPAND IN '97.

text.p: Deutsche Bank Polska SA, year-old Polish subsidiary of Germany's Deutsche Bank AG , will reach break-even next year and aims to open branches outside Warsaw, its chairman Georg Krupp said on Tuesday.
"In the second year of our activity in Poland, in 1997, we will reach break-even," Krupp told a news conference.
"This is an extraordinary achievement and a...basis for deciding whether to emerge on the territory of the whole country," Krupp said.
He said that the bank would consider branches in Poznan, Gdansk, Szczecin, Katowice and Wroclaw.
Although Deutsche Bank Polska (DBP) had a sophisticated electronic banking system working in Poland, it wanted direct contact with clients beyond its Warsaw base, he said.
He declined to reveal anticipated results figures.
Krupp said the bank would gradually increase its offer.
"We see big possibilities in leasing and in operations on the capital market in Poland," he said.
"In a further perspective, we also aim to offer savings systems for financing construction and insurance systems on this market," he said.

He said that for housing savings and insurance business the bank would not open independent companies in Poland, especially as it did not plan to build its own network of outlets, but would base itself on Deutsche Bank AG's German subsidiaries and on cooperation and providing know-how to Polish companies.
The bank was now setting up a leasing company in Poland, in cooperation with Deutsche Bank group's trade credit firm GEFA.
"Leasing in Poland is comparatively weakly developed and we anticipate that it will soon grow dynamically," he said.
It was also issuing Eurocard Gold and Eurocard Business credit cards, he added.

Officials of the bank said that it had tripled its own capital to 135 million zlotys from 45 million and was one of the few banks in Poland to have access to long-term funds from the Luxembourg-based European Investment Bank.
They said more than 200 firms were banking with DBP, which had over 40 corresponding banks in Poland.
Krupp said the bank had pioneered the use of options on currency markets in Poland.
"The German mark's share in overall currency transactions in Poland has risen since DBP entered the market from 10 percent to 25 percent. More than half of these transactions fall to DBP," he said.

He said the bank was expanding its activity on Polish capital markets through its investment banking branch Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, which in July led the Polish government's successful 250 million mark eurobond issue.
In March DBP got permission from the Polish central bank to operate on the primary market, allowing it to take part directly in treasury auctions. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
